# PhotoFindry

**Find the photo you remember. Keep your photos on your computer.**

PhotoFindry tags and searches photographs locally on Apple-silicon Mac, Linux x86-64 and Windows x64. It installs a background companion and opens its workspace in your browser. Your originals, selected models and library stay on your computer. Official builds are free, with no subscription or PhotoFindry account.

## Install the current beta

**Mac: 0.3.0-beta.5 · build 138** — [release notes and downloads](https://github.com/sentrybottale/photofindryapp/releases/tag/v0.3.0-beta.5). **Linux: 0.3.0-beta.3 · build 136** and **Windows: 0.3.0-beta.2 · build 132** remain available from their signed platform feeds.

Choose the instructions for the computer where you will run PhotoFindry:

| Your computer | Before installing | Installation guide | Open it afterward |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **Mac with Apple silicon** | macOS 14 or later; Intel Macs are not supported | [Mac: Terminal setup](INSTALLATION.md#macos-apple-silicon) | [Open PhotoFindry](https://app.photofindry.com/) |
| **Windows 10/11, x64** | Microsoft Visual C++ v14 **x64** runtime and a working Vulkan graphics driver | [Windows: PowerShell setup](INSTALLATION.md#windows-x64) | PhotoFindry in the Start menu |
| **Linux, x86-64** | A systemd user session and the listed command-line tools; `zenity` for the desktop folder chooser | [Linux: terminal setup](INSTALLATION.md#linux-x86-64) | Applications menu or `photofindry open` |

1. Open your platform's guide above and check its prerequisites.
2. Copy the **whole verified setup block** into Terminal or PowerShell. Run PhotoFindry setup as your normal user, without `sudo` or **Run as administrator**. The command checks its installer before running it, then installs the publisher-authenticated companion and login startup.
3. When the local browser workspace opens, choose your vision model and matching projector, add a small photo folder, and start tagging. The [first-run checklist](INSTALLATION.md#after-installation) explains what to expect.

You do not need to clone this repository, compile the client, or download the GitHub **Source code** archives to use PhotoFindry. Fresh Mac users install the CLI companion directly; the older Mac application's only installation role is [migrating existing app users](INSTALLATION.md#existing-mac-app-users).

## Downloads, updates and recovery

The setup commands follow the signed feed for your platform and install the latest compatible published build. Their pinned script addresses stay the same across later releases. See [which release files to use](INSTALLATION.md#which-release-files-do-i-need) if you are browsing the release assets.

Use **Settings → Background companion** for update, startup and recovery controls. Updates replace program files while preserving your library, original photos, saved work and selected model paths. If PhotoFindry cannot open, [rerun the verified setup for your platform](INSTALLATION.md#updates-and-recovery); do not delete your library to repair startup.

First-install trust matters: independently trust the setup instructions, immutable script/verifier hashes and existing publisher key. A checksum copied with a compromised download does not authenticate itself. Read [verification](VERIFY.md). Mac packages use ad-hoc code sealing and separate publisher Ed25519 signatures.

## What is included

- **Local tagging and search.** Select compatible vision GGUF weights and their matching multimodal projector separately; model files can stay in any folder. Search models are bundled.
- **People on Mac and Linux.** Windows does not yet include the face provider.
- **Platform-specific features.** Whole-library backup and restore work across Mac, Linux and Windows; source archives and dedicated CLEF/Intern review runtimes remain Mac-only. See [platform differences and tested scope](INSTALLATION.md#platform-differences).
- **Your originals stay in place.** Cached previews are not backups of original photographs. Keep independent backups.

The clean [client snapshot](client/) is MIT, covering the browser UI, native launcher, companion bridge and allowlisted interaction helpers. Rust engine cores and worker implementations remain proprietary. The implementation repository and history remain private. See [licensing](LICENSE), [privacy](PRIVACY.md) and the [client source inventory](client/CLIENT-SOURCE.json).

[Installation and troubleshooting](INSTALLATION.md) · [Getting started](docs/getting-started.md) · [Website](https://photofindry.com) · [Private feedback](https://photofindry.com/bugs) · [Optional support](https://buymeacoffee.com/photorecall)

# Install PhotoFindry

**Mac: 0.3.0-beta.5 · build 138. Linux: 0.3.0-beta.3 · build 136. Windows: 0.3.0-beta.2 · build 132.** Installation guide updated 31 October 2026.

PhotoFindry installs a local background companion and opens a browser workspace. The public website does not receive your photos or library session. You do not need a PhotoFindry account, a subscription, a compiler, or a checkout of this repository.

**Jump to your platform:** [Mac](#macos-apple-silicon) · [Windows](#windows-x64) · [Linux](#linux-x86-64)

[First run](#after-installation) · [Release files](#which-release-files-do-i-need) · [Updates and recovery](#updates-and-recovery) · [Older Mac apps](#existing-mac-app-users) · [Troubleshooting](#installation-troubleshooting)

## Choose the right version

| Platform | Supported architecture | Requirements |
| --- | --- | --- |
| macOS | **Apple silicon / arm64** | macOS 14+; Core ML semantic ranking needs macOS 15+ |
| Windows | **Intel/AMD x64 / x86_64** | Windows 10/11; Visual C++ v14 x64 runtime; working Vulkan graphics driver |
| Linux | **Intel/AMD x86-64 / x86_64** | systemd user session; Bash, curl, tar, sha256sum, base64 and systemctl; zenity for the desktop chooser |

There is no Intel Mac or ARM Linux/Windows package. On Mac, **Apple menu → About This Mac** should show an Apple chip. On Windows, check **Settings → System → About → System type** for an x64-based processor. On Linux, `uname -m` should report `x86_64`.

Allow disk space for the program, your chosen model and projector, and library previews. Model memory and performance needs vary; the package download sizes below do not include your chosen vision model. Start with a small folder and keep independent backups of originals.

The commands below use immutable, checksum-pinned setup scripts. Each script then checks its pinned verifier and the platform's publisher-signed release feed before installing the package. **Copy the entire block, including the checksum check.** For first installation, independently trust these instructions and the existing publisher pin in the [verification guide](https://github.com/sentrybottale/photofindryapp/blob/main/VERIFY.md). Do not bypass a failed checksum or accept an unexplained key change.

## macOS (Apple silicon)

### Before you start

Use an Apple-silicon Mac running macOS 14 or later. Normal setup uses macOS's included tools; it does not require Xcode or the Swift compiler. You do not drag an application into Applications for a fresh install.

### Install

1. Open **Terminal** from Applications → Utilities, or search for Terminal with Spotlight.
2. Copy the entire block below, paste it into Terminal and press Return. Run it as your normal account, without `sudo`.
3. Wait for verification, download and installation to finish. The local workspace opens in your default browser. You can close Terminal after setup finishes; the companion continues running.

```sh
( pf_setup=$(/usr/bin/mktemp) || exit
trap '/bin/rm -f "$pf_setup"' EXIT
/usr/bin/curl --disable -fL --proto '=https' --proto-redir '=https' --max-time 60 --max-filesize 65536 https://photofindry.com/installers/sha256/588a19f4d9be78372921c2c2e2ee43f4df04bb127388c5849f980eef7f49c522/install-cli.sh -o "$pf_setup" || { /bin/echo 'PhotoFindry setup could not download. Check your connection, then retry. Your library was not changed.' >&2; exit 1; }
printf '588a19f4d9be78372921c2c2e2ee43f4df04bb127388c5849f980eef7f49c522  %s\n' "$pf_setup" | /usr/bin/shasum -a 256 -c - || { /bin/echo 'PhotoFindry setup did not match its trusted checksum. Nothing was run. Get the complete setup command from https://photofindry.com/docs/install.html and retry.' >&2; exit 1; }
/usr/bin/env -i HOME="$HOME" PATH=/usr/bin:/bin:/usr/sbin:/sbin /bin/bash "$pf_setup" )
```

### Open it again

Visit [app.photofindry.com](https://app.photofindry.com/) and choose **Open PhotoFindry**. Allow your browser to open the local PhotoFindry link if asked. The address changes to the local workspace. Login startup is installed automatically and can be changed in **Settings → Background companion**.

When **Files** asks for a source folder, select the existing originals folder in the native chooser. The retained local access helper keeps that choice across routine updates. If macOS access is revoked, use the specific folder-access action shown in Files; do not delete permission files or originals.

Already using an older native Mac app? See [Existing Mac app users](#existing-mac-app-users).

## Windows (x64)

### Before you start

1. Install Microsoft's **Visual C++ v14 Redistributable, x64**: [official Microsoft downloads and requirements](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/cpp/windows/latest-supported-vc-redist) · [x64 installer](https://aka.ms/vc14/vc_redist.x64.exe). You need the runtime, not the Visual Studio development environment. Microsoft's installer may request administrator approval.
2. Install or update the graphics driver supplied by your GPU manufacturer so Vulkan is available.
3. Use a normal **64-bit Windows PowerShell** window. PhotoFindry setup itself must not run as administrator. The setup uses Windows's `curl.exe` and `tar.exe`.

### Install

1. Open Start, type **Windows PowerShell**, and open it normally. Do not choose **Run as administrator**. If using Windows Terminal, select its Windows PowerShell tab rather than Command Prompt.
2. Copy the whole block below, paste it into PowerShell and press Enter. If the terminal asks about pasting multiple lines, review the block before allowing the paste.
3. Wait until setup reports **Ready**. It installs startup for your account and opens the local browser workspace. You can close PowerShell after setup finishes.

```powershell
$pfSetup = Join-Path ([IO.Path]::GetTempPath()) ('photofindry-' + [guid]::NewGuid().ToString('N') + '.ps1')
try {
  curl.exe --disable -fL --proto '=https' --proto-redir '=https' --max-time 60 --max-filesize 65536 'https://photofindry.com/installers/sha256/24203d48b8b86da3c782e8afa94df000dbf2a8a7aadaa49197e2d58e6d17cefa/install-windows.ps1' -o $pfSetup
  if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) { throw 'PhotoFindry setup could not download.' }
  if ((Get-FileHash -LiteralPath $pfSetup -Algorithm SHA256).Hash.ToLowerInvariant() -ne '24203d48b8b86da3c782e8afa94df000dbf2a8a7aadaa49197e2d58e6d17cefa') { throw 'PhotoFindry setup checksum did not match. Nothing was run.' }
  powershell.exe -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File $pfSetup
  if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) { throw 'PhotoFindry setup did not finish. Your library is kept.' }
} finally { Remove-Item -LiteralPath $pfSetup -Force -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue }
```

The command's execution-policy option applies to the setup child process; it does not change your machine's saved execution-policy setting. On a managed PC, follow your organization's policy if script execution is blocked.

### Open it again

Open **PhotoFindry** from the **Start menu**. The installed companion runs locally and opens the browser interface. It starts when you sign in unless you disable startup in the companion settings.

Windows has no People/face provider, source archives or dedicated CLEF/Intern review runtime. Portable whole-library backup and restore are available. The configured vision model is selected separately during first run.

## Linux (x86-64)

### Before you start

Use your normal account in a session with a working systemd user manager. The installer checks for `curl`, `tar`, `sha256sum`, `base64` and `systemctl`; Bash is required to run it. Install missing tools using your distribution's package manager before running setup. Install `zenity` for the native desktop folder chooser and use a desktop browser for the local workspace. Optional HEIF/AVIF decoding needs system libheif codecs.

You can check the user manager without changing it:

```sh
systemctl --user show-environment
```

If that command fails, log in to a session with a systemd user manager before continuing. Do not run PhotoFindry setup through `sudo` or from a root shell.

### Install

1. Open your desktop terminal.
2. Copy the complete block below, paste it into the terminal and run it as your normal user.
3. Wait for verification, download and the **Ready** message. Setup installs the user service and opens the browser when desktop opening is available.

```bash
( pf_setup=$(mktemp) || exit
trap 'rm -f "$pf_setup"' EXIT
curl --disable -fL --proto '=https' --proto-redir '=https' --max-time 60 --max-filesize 65536 'https://photofindry.com/installers/sha256/9db6253cb7d39340d98b65df562516997bb82081fd8cea4b2be32005c91ef857/install-linux.sh' -o "$pf_setup" || exit 1
printf '9db6253cb7d39340d98b65df562516997bb82081fd8cea4b2be32005c91ef857  %s\n' "$pf_setup" | sha256sum -c - || exit 1
bash "$pf_setup" )
```

### Open it again

Choose **PhotoFindry** from your applications menu, or run:

```sh
photofindry open
```

If the browser did not open automatically, use that installed entry again. If your shell cannot find `photofindry`, use the applications menu and check your user PATH configuration. The installer also prints the full installed executable path for status checks.

Linux core installation and real-model checks were performed on an x86-64 Ubuntu system. Those headless tests do not establish a fully qualified Linux desktop GUI or performance on every GPU and distribution.

## After installation

1. **Open the local workspace.** Use your platform's installed entry. Its address is local, typically `http://127.0.0.1:…`; the port can change, so use the Open entry instead of depending on a bookmark to an old port.
2. **Choose your model files.** In model setup or **Settings → Local models**, select a compatible vision **GGUF** and its matching **multimodal projector**. The projector must match the model. Keep both files in any folder you choose; you do not have to move them into the program directory. Search models are bundled, while an optional search reranker is selected or explicitly downloaded separately.
3. **Add a small source folder in Files.** Choose the existing originals folder with the platform picker. Original photographs stay in place. Cloud-backed originals need to be available locally when processing reads them.
4. **Start tagging.** Adding a folder alone does not establish that it has accepted tags. Follow progress in Jobs. Saved jobs may reopen paused; choose Resume when you want them to continue.
5. **Try ordinary search, then Local AI Search.** Ordinary search uses saved information. Local AI Search is an explicit model-assisted action.
6. **Check Settings/About** for the installed version and background companion status. For the current release, expect **0.3.0-beta.5 / build 138** on Mac, **0.3.0-beta.3 / build 136** on Linux or **0.3.0-beta.2 / build 132** on Windows; a later signed release may be installed by the same setup command.

See [Getting started](https://github.com/sentrybottale/photofindryapp/blob/main/docs/getting-started.md) and [Search](https://github.com/sentrybottale/photofindryapp/blob/main/docs/search.md) for the full workflow.

## Which release files do I need?

**For normal installation, use the verified setup block above.** It selects and verifies the correct package, registers the companion and installs startup. Downloading a ZIP alone does not perform those steps.

The current program archives are:

| Platform | Program archive | Download size, excluding your vision model |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Apple-silicon Mac | [`PhotoFindry-0.3.0-beta.5-arm64-companion.zip`](https://github.com/sentrybottale/photofindryapp/releases/tag/v0.3.0-beta.5) | 398,600,794 bytes (about 399 MB) |
| Linux x86-64 | [`PhotoFindry-0.3.0-beta.3-linux-x86_64-companion.tar.gz`](https://github.com/sentrybottale/photofindryapp/releases/tag/v0.3.0-beta.3) | 364,454,429 bytes (about 364 MB) |
| Windows x64 | [`PhotoFindry-0.3.0-beta.2-windows-x86_64-companion.zip`](https://github.com/sentrybottale/photofindryapp/releases/tag/v0.3.0-beta.2) | 87,222,087 bytes (about 87 MB) |

Other assets have different purposes:

| Files | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `install-cli.sh`, `install-linux.sh`, `install-windows.ps1` | Reviewable setup scripts. Use the pinned commands above to verify them before execution. |
| `cli-release.json`, `cli-linux-x86_64-release.json`, `cli-windows-x86_64-release.json` | Signed release metadata used by the installer/updater; not applications to open. |
| `SHA256SUMS.txt`, `SHA256SUMS.ed25519`, verifier binaries and verification guides | Download authenticity/integrity checks. See the verification guide before manual installation. |
| `photofindry-client-source.tar.gz`, `CLIENT-SOURCE.json`, GitHub **Source code (zip/tar.gz)** | Source and inventory for developers; not ready-to-run installers and not the proprietary engine source. |
| `QUALIFICATION.md`, notices and component maps | Tested scope, limitations and licensing information. |
| `qualification-prior-…-release.json` | Test-baseline metadata, not a user installation or downgrade channel. |
| Older Mac DMG/update ZIP assets | The retained native-app migration channel; not fresh CLI installation. |

**Choosing an older release:** the setup blocks follow the current signed feed; they do not pin installation to the version of this guide or an old release page. Do not edit a version number or remove signature checks to force a downgrade. For recovery, use the retained previous verified companion when offered in Settings. A manual historical installation needs that release's instructions and confirmed saved-data compatibility.

## Updates and recovery

In the local workspace, open **Settings → Background companion** to manage startup, update checks and recovery. Background checks do not install by themselves. Explicit **Open PhotoFindry** checks the authenticated feed and can install a newer signed build when owned work can safely drain; offline or busy conditions keep the verified current build usable with a visible reason. You can also choose **Install signed update**.

Updates replace the program, preserving libraries, original photographs, saved work and selected model paths. Accepted maintenance runs independently of the requesting browser or terminal. Closing that requester does not cancel the update.

If PhotoFindry cannot start, **rerun the complete verified setup block for your platform**. It follows the registered library and repairs the program without needing the broken companion to open. Keep the library in place, including a custom data location. If another app still owns it, finish or pause work and quit that app before retrying.

Use **Recover companion** or **Use previous companion version** in Settings when offered. On Mac the native opening helper can offer **Recover and open**. Software recovery never means restoring an older library backup automatically. Do not delete databases, originals or models to repair startup.

## Existing Mac app users

This section is only for users of the older native Mac application. Fresh Mac users should use the CLI setup above.

1. In the older app, choose **PhotoFindry → Check for Updates** to receive the retained one-time migration bridge.
2. If its updater is unavailable, use the [beta 16 migration bridge](https://github.com/sentrybottale/photofindryapp/releases/download/v0.2.0-beta.16/PhotoFindry-0.2.0-beta.16-arm64-community-beta.dmg), following the [verification guide](https://github.com/sentrybottale/photofindryapp/blob/main/VERIFY.md). This is a separate migration channel, not the current fresh-install package.
3. Let the bridge prepare its verified recovery copy and hand the registered library to the independent companion. It keeps existing data and model paths, opens the browser when ready, and exits.
4. After a successful handoff, use the companion's Open entry. The migration app is no longer the permanent host and can be moved to Trash.

**Use current beta** remains the alternative before migration and after a failure. It opens the retained verified native version without restoring old library data. Read the migration screen before continuing and keep the recovery copy.

## Installation troubleshooting

| What you see | What to do |
| --- | --- |
| Checksum mismatch or **FAILED** | Stop. Nothing should be run from that download. Copy the full current block again; never remove its checksum check. |
| Publisher/signature verification failed | Keep the installed library and software. Check your connection and the official instructions; do not accept a different key to get past the error. |
| Windows reports a missing Microsoft runtime DLL | Install or repair Microsoft's Visual C++ v14 **x64** runtime, then rerun the complete setup block. Do not download individual DLLs from third-party sites. |
| Windows setup says to use a normal user | Close the elevated PowerShell window and reopen Windows PowerShell normally. |
| Linux reports a missing tool or user manager | Install the named dependency, or log in to a session where `systemctl --user show-environment` works. Rerun as your normal user. |
| Linux has no folder chooser | Install `zenity` and use a desktop session. |
| Browser opens an old address or fails to connect | Use the Mac Open link, Windows Start menu, or Linux installed entry again instead of a saved localhost port. If necessary, rerun the verified setup. |
| Another app owns the library | Finish or pause its work, quit that app and retry. Keep its library and lock files. |
| Model or original file unavailable | Select its existing location in Settings or Files. An offline external drive is not a reason to delete saved data. |
| A job is paused | Review its reason and choose Resume when appropriate. Reinstalling should not be used to erase or restart saved work. |

Further help: [Troubleshooting guide](https://github.com/sentrybottale/photofindryapp/blob/main/docs/troubleshooting.md) · [Private feedback](https://photofindry.com/bugs). Share the error and platform; do not post private photos, library databases or model traces in public issues.

## Platform differences

People is included on Mac and Linux; Windows has no face provider. Whole-library backup and restore work across Mac, Linux and Windows. Source archives and dedicated CLEF/Intern review runtimes remain Mac-only. Keep independent backups of originals on every platform; previews are reduced cached copies, not original-photo backups.

macOS 14 is the declared minimum, with macOS 27.0 used for the published qualification. Linux/Windows core trials used small real-evidence libraries; they do not establish every desktop, codec, GPU or full-library performance combination. Read each release's QUALIFICATION.md ([Mac 0.3.0-beta.5](https://github.com/sentrybottale/photofindryapp/releases/download/v0.3.0-beta.5/QUALIFICATION.md), [Linux 0.3.0-beta.3](https://github.com/sentrybottale/photofindryapp/releases/download/v0.3.0-beta.3/QUALIFICATION.md), [Windows 0.3.0-beta.2](https://github.com/sentrybottale/photofindryapp/releases/download/v0.3.0-beta.2/QUALIFICATION.md)) for the actual tested scope.

# PhotoFindry 0.3.0-beta.5 · build 138

This hotfix updates the Mac companion. Linux keeps 0.3.0-beta.3 / build 136 and Windows keeps 0.3.0-beta.2 / build 132.

Reconnecting originals is fast again. A library restored from another computer, or a folder chosen at a new location, reconnects each photo by its relative location, size and dates, without reading or downloading the original. Choosing a folder no longer reads every photo once to record a checksum. Background checks handle many more photos per step, so large cloud folders finish in minutes instead of hours.

Ordinary search is faster without changing its results. Searches for people words such as woman or girl return in roughly a third to half of the previous time, later pages of Related results load almost immediately instead of repeating the whole search, and refreshing stale saved projections after an upgrade commits in groups. Matches, order and Related coverage are unchanged. A running search also keeps going while background checks reconnect originals, unless the photos in its scope or their saved details actually change. Refreshing an outdated saved search entry now keeps the semantic index of every unchanged line. Known limit, unchanged from build 137: photos indexed under an older evidence format still lose most of their semantic index when an ordinary search for words such as man or woman refreshes them, and while the queue is paused Local AI Search reports limited coverage and can omit them until the queue is resumed. A fix is planned for the next build.

A file replaced at the same location still gets a new change time: it is compared against its saved checksum, or listed for review, and its saved tags are not transferred. No library migration, retagging or extra folder review is required.

Updates preserve the library, originals, model paths and saved work. All inference remains local. The MIT client excludes proprietary engine source and private development history. The beta 16 Mac-app migration channel is unchanged.

See QUALIFICATION.md for the exact candidate evidence and hardware limits. Public delivery is complete only after the delivered-byte, live-feed, installer, recovery and website checks pass.


---

# PhotoFindry 0.3.0-beta.5 / build 138 qualification

This hotfix updates the Mac companion. Linux retains its signed 0.3.0-beta.3 / build 136 release and Windows retains 0.3.0-beta.2 / build 132. The existing beta 16 Mac-app migration channel is unchanged.

## Change

Build 137 still re-read originals in three cases: a library restored from another computer whose saved paths point elsewhere, a network mount that reports no volume identity, and choosing a folder, which read every photo once to record a checksum. Build 138 reconnects all three by each photo's relative location, size, modification time and change time, without reading or downloading original contents. A matching byte comparison now updates the saved proof, so the next return of that folder reads nothing. An original that cannot be read keeps its location and becomes available, still without a content read, once access returns. Background source checks process larger bounded steps and publish source/job notices at most every two seconds.

Ordinary search keeps its matches, order and Related coverage while doing less work: people-word searches reuse change tokens and coverage data, later Related pages reuse the first page's work, and stale saved projections are refreshed in grouped commits. A running Local AI Search is no longer stopped by background checks that only rewrite saved locations or re-encode unchanged saved text; changes to the photos in its scope still stop it. Refreshing an outdated saved projection keeps the saved vector of any unchanged evidence text; previously a people-word search re-projected such photos with empty vectors, removing them from Local AI Search retrieval until background indexing ran. The Karate user-journey suite found this; see Limits for the part that remains.

A file replaced at the same location still gets a new change time. It is compared against its saved checksum, or listed for review, and its saved tags are not transferred. No library migration, retagging or folder review is required.

## Exact candidate checks

The signed lifecycle passed all 17 checks from the published build 137 to candidate 138: upgrade, rollback, anti-replay, signature rejection, interrupted switch recovery, serving policy and preserved-data uninstall/reinstall. The complete Mac source matrix passed against the exact package: 1,616 JavaScript tests with 1,588 passes, zero failures and 28 optional skips; 248 Python tests (two opt-in skips); 864 Rust tests with zero failures (14 ignored); and the Swift build.

The installed candidate passed the real-core checks on a 93,807-photo isolated library on an Apple M5 MacBook Pro with 32 GiB RAM and macOS 27.0.1, using Qwen3.5 4B Q4_K_M with its matching BF16 projector and Qwen3 reranker 0.6B Q8:

| Check | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Ordinary search | 6,883 matches; 3.42 s |
| Completed scoped AI | 1 candidate; 58.34 s |
| Real tagging | 1 copied photograph; 32 observations; 50.90 s |
| Whole-pool retrieval to saved scores | 22,191 candidates; 70.80 s |
| Active Stop | 1.81 s; saved results retained |
| Recovery, retained folder-access owner, uninstall | Completed results reopened; 93,807 photos and all unfinished jobs preserved |

These timings were taken while other qualification work shared the same Mac and are not throughput claims.

The Karate user-journey suite ran against the exact signed package on a separate copy of the same library: 5 of 6 scenarios passed (two source remount scenarios, job control, install/update/uninstall lifecycle and the imported library). Reconnecting 3,000 photos took 4.16 s and read 1.4 MB of 224.6 MB of original bytes. The tagging, search and AI scenario failed its whole-library floor: after a people-word search for a newly tagged photo, Local AI Search returned 21,168 candidates instead of at least 22,000 and correctly reported limited semantic coverage. Build 137 behaves the same way (21,043 before this build's change); see Limits.

## Limits

Provider-side substitutions that preserve size, modification time and change time are not detected without an explicit content comparison. A people-word ordinary search refreshes outdated saved projections. Photos indexed under an older evidence format change almost every line when refreshed, so they lose most saved vectors until background semantic indexing runs; while the queue is paused, Local AI Search reports limited semantic coverage and can omit them (on the isolated library, 1,016 such photos after one search). Resuming the queue re-indexes them. This is unchanged from build 137 and is planned for the next build. The isolated fixture's cloud folders are checked against live provider metadata; a full scan of every original is not claimed complete. Another Mac, Linux and Windows are not covered by these build 138 receipts.

## Public delivery

Candidate results do not qualify public downloads. Publication requires fresh anonymous asset/signature verification, the live feed, installed public update/core/Stop/recovery, required source/churn tests, the exact served installer command and both websites. Completion is recorded only after those delivered-byte checks pass.


---

# Privacy, licensing and direct beta distribution

PhotoFindry’s client is MIT open source; its Rust engine cores remain proprietary. Official builds are free for personal and business use. There is no mandatory app account, subscription, advertising analytics or app telemetry. Optional [Buy Me a Coffee support](https://buymeacoffee.com/photorecall) does not unlock features.

## Local photo work

Photo tagging, face processing and search inference run locally on your computer. People is available on Mac and Linux. Original photographs stay in their folders. Local saved work remains readable and exportable. Mac backups and source archives exclude original photographs and model weights; keep your own backups of those files.

The current app is not an OS-enforced network sandbox, and local processing is not a guarantee that software has no security defects. Downloads, update checks, browser links and voluntary feedback require network connections. After migration, background CLI update checks are on by default and can be turned off under Settings → Background companion; they contact the fixed host after startup and about every six hours while the companion runs, but do not install by themselves. Every explicit Open checks that fixed publisher-authenticated feed and installs a newer signed build before opening when saved work can safely drain. Offline checks and active foreground work keep the verified current version open with a local explanation. Older app versions retain their signed app feed for the one-time transition. Checks do not send photos, search queries or library records; hosts receive ordinary connection information. First installation remains your choice.

## Voluntary feedback

The form at photofindry.com/bugs sends your required email, typed report and chosen screenshots over HTTPS to the PhotoFindry server for private review and follow-up. It returns a reference only after storage succeeds. Server copies remove original screenshot metadata and filenames; visible image content remains visible. Redact private details before uploading.

No photo library, saved queries or diagnostic logs are collected automatically. Reports remain until the team explicitly removes them. Reports and screenshots are private and accessible only to the PhotoFindry team. Short-lived keyed network identifiers limit abuse. The feedback form has no analytics or advertising trackers.

Send Feedback submits directly to this private service and returns a report reference. Earlier beta 2 builds used an email draft; update to use direct native submission.

## Website and app are distinct

The marketing homepage uses optional PostHog website analytics only after you accept analytics cookies. PostHog uses an EU endpoint and identified-only profiles. Session recording and automatic interaction capture are disabled. The app.photofindry.com entry hub has its own explicit analytics consent, without replay, automatic interaction capture or person profiles. It never receives local-library authority. Neither website consent grants consent for localhost analytics. The documentation pages and feedback form do not load this analytics script. Infrastructure may maintain operational connection logs; “no app tracking” is not a promise that no server can observe a network request.

## Why a direct companion rather than Apple's stores?

PhotoFindry is distributed directly: a signed command-line companion from the official GitHub release, updated through its own Ed25519-signed feed, with the browser as its interface. This is a distribution decision, not a claim that any software is automatically safe.

The app bundle is ad-hoc signed. Separate pinned Ed25519 signatures authenticate the release inventory, update feed and archive. They establish approved bytes and possession of the signing key, not absence of vulnerabilities. Follow the official verification and per-app installation guidance.

The public [photofindryapp repository](https://github.com/sentrybottale/photofindryapp) contains the MIT client snapshot, distribution documentation and official binaries. The private development history and engine implementation stay private. Third-party licences and notices remain included. Read the [licence](https://github.com/sentrybottale/photofindryapp/blob/main/LICENSE) and [qualification record](https://github.com/sentrybottale/photofindryapp/blob/main/QUALIFICATION.md).

## Optional diagnostic attachment

The feedback form includes an unchecked **Include diagnostic log with this report** option in the app feedback form. It includes up to 200 recent operational events from the current session, covering at most 30 minutes. It contains selected job/model states and numeric progress, memory and token counters, excluding raw messages, names, filenames, queries, paths, photo identifiers and image content. It is not a full crash log.

Opting in freezes the attachment for review. Refresh log captures a newer copy; unchecking removes it. Only Submit Feedback sends the reviewed attachment. Retries reuse that copy. Earlier sessions and historical disk logs are not collected. Diagnostic attachments stay with the private report and follow the same retention policy.

## Cookies and storage

The homepage offers **Accept all**, **Reject optional** and **Settings**. Optional analytics stays off until you accept it; rejecting it does not affect downloads or other site features. Change or withdraw your choice using **Cookie settings** in the homepage footer or [open cookie settings](https://photofindry.com/#cookie-settings).

A necessary first-party cookie, `photofindry_consent_v1`, remembers your choice for 180 days on this site only. If you accept analytics, PostHog may store a first-party browser identifier in cookies and local storage to measure visits. Its cookies last up to 180 days; local storage persists until cleared. Rejecting analytics removes this site's PostHog cookies and browser storage and stops further collection; it does not erase information already sent. Do Not Track is respected.

If JavaScript is disabled, optional analytics does not load. Documentation and the feedback form do not load analytics. These website choices do not enable tracking in the Mac app.


---

# Verify a release

PhotoFindry publishes a **SHA256SUMS.txt** inventory and its detached Ed25519
signature, **SHA256SUMS.ed25519**, with every release. This authenticates the
listed bytes against the PhotoFindry update-signing key. A checksum by itself
only detects differing bytes; it does not establish who published them.

The pinned public key is:

```text
G363x/YCT07qbJyyI5minQjp3v+6SEw9sB7dU3pL6cM=
```

It is also recorded in this repository's `update-verification.json` and the app.
Keep a trusted copy. Downloading a replacement key, verification program and
artifacts from the same compromised source would not establish trust. Do not
accept an unexplained key change.

## Full signature and checksum verification

The small [verify-release.swift](verify-release.swift) utility uses Apple's
CryptoKit, contains only public verification data, and makes no network requests.
It requires Apple's Command Line Tools with Swift; they are not required to run
PhotoFindry itself. You can inspect this standalone utility before running it.

1. Download `SHA256SUMS.txt`, `SHA256SUMS.ed25519`, and **all files named in the
   inventory** from the same official release into a new folder.
2. Save `verify-release.swift` from the release repository in that folder. Confirm
   its embedded public key matches your trusted key above.
3. In Terminal, change to that folder and run:

```sh
swift verify-release.swift .
```

Success reports a verified signature and matching hashes for every listed file.
A failure means the files have not been verified; do not install them. Verification
does not run the application. This utility is separate release tooling, not
application or engine source.

For an additional ordinary byte check, macOS also supports:

```sh
shasum -a 256 -c SHA256SUMS.txt
```

That command alone does **not** check the signature or publisher.

## Application updates

Older app versions authenticate the one-time migration installer using the retained
signed app feed at `https://photofindry.com/updates/beta/appcast.xml`. After handoff,
the independent CLI uses `https://photofindry.com/updates/cli/release.json`.
Its Ed25519 envelope authenticates release/build/platform/data contract, archive
URL/size/hash and the complete package inventory. The installed verifier contains
the same trusted publisher pin; the server cannot supply a replacement key.

Settings → Background companion controls login startup and background checks.
Background checks do not install by themselves. Every explicit Open checks the
fixed authenticated feed and installs a newer signed CLI build when saved work
can safely drain. Offline checks or active work keep the verified current
build open with a visible deferred-update reason. You can also choose Install
signed update. Failed or interrupted switches retain verified prior software
and never automatically restore an older library. The local opening helper
offers Recover and open.

The companion’s native executables use ad-hoc macOS code seals. These are distinct from the
maintainer's Ed25519 download/update signatures and do not provide Apple publisher
validation. Signature verification proves possession of the signing key and exact bytes, not absence of
bugs, enforced isolation or a security guarantee.
